'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**A [[Hamas]] rocket kills two [[Thai people|Thai]] workers and injures ten others in southern [[Israel]], thereby bringing the death toll in the country to 12. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/2-thai-workers-killed-several-people-injured-as-hamas-bombards-southern-israel/ (''Times of Israel'')]
**The death toll from the Israeli airstrikes in Gaza rise to at least 217 Palestinians killed, including 63 children. About 1,500 others have been wounded. Gaza's main [[COVID-19]] laboratory is destroyed by a strike, stopping all COVID-19 tests as a result. Four more protesters are also killed in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/18/israel-shells-lebanon-as-biden-continues-push-for-gaza-ceasefire (Al Jazeera)]
**The [[Israeli Defense Forces|IDF]] reports the death of 160 Hamas and Islamic Jihad members. However, the deaths are not confirmed by either the groups or Palestinian authorities, who reported a lower number of militants killed. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/idf-ships-eliminate-targets-off-coast-of-gaza-strip-report-668385?utm_source=spotim&utm_medium=spotim_recirculation (Jerusalem Post)]
**Israeli police fire [[stun grenade]]s, [[rubber bullet]]s, and spray [[Skunk (weapon)|skunk water]] at protesters gathered at the [[Damascus Gate]] in [[Jerusalem]]'s [[Old City (Jerusalem)|Old City]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/palestinian-protesters-dodge-stun-grenades-and-skunk-spray-as-skirmishes-spread-through-jerusalems-old-city-12310144 (''Sky News'')]
**One Palestinian is killed and dozens more are wounded after Israeli security forces open fire on protesters marching at a [[Security checkpoint|military checkpoint]] in the [[Beit El]] [[Israeli settlement|settlement]] in the [[West Bank]]. Further clashes are also reported in [[Hebron]], [[Bethlehem]], [[Nablus]], and [[Budrus]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/18/palestinian-fighters-engage-israel-soldiers-in-west-bank-gunfire (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in the Maghreb (2002–present)|Insurgency in the Maghreb]]
**Gunmen storm a church during a [[baptism]] in a village in [[Burkina Faso]] and open fire, killing 15 people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/armed-men-kill-15-baptism-northern-burkina-faso-2021-05-19/ (Reuters)]
*Spillover of the [[Moro conflict]]
**Five [[Abu Sayyaf]] militants are killed during a [[shootout]] with police in [[Beaufort, Malaysia|Beaufort]], [[Sabah]], [[Malaysia]]. All of those killed are [[Filipinos]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/18/malaysia-police-kill-suspected-abu-sayyaf-fighters-during-raid (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan clashes|2021 Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan conflict]]
**Officials in [[Kyrgyzstan]] and [[Tajikistan]] announce that they have agreed to joint security controls following clashes between the two countries at [[Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border|the border]]. [https://www.rferl.org/a/kyrgyzstan-tajikistan-agree-to-joint-security-controls-along-disputed-border-/31261592.html (RFERL)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The first semifinal round of the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2021]] takes place in [[Rotterdam]]. [https://eurovision.tv/story/dates-for-eurovision-2021-announced (Eurovision.tv)]

'''Business and economy'''
*Three [[China|Chinese]] industry associations announce in a joint statement that financial institutions and payment firms are banned from offering services related to [[cryptocurrency]] transactions, highlighting their high volatility. China had previously banned or restricted access to [[cryptocurrency exchange]]s, and blocked websites that had [[initial coin offering]]s.  [https://www.reuters.com/technology/chinese-financial-payment-bodies-barred-cryptocurrency-business-2021-05-18/ (Reuters)] 

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Cyclone Tauktae]]
**At least 26 people are dead and 53 more are missing after an [[ONGC]] [[barge|barge P305]] sailing off the coast of [[Mumbai]], [[India]] sank during severe weather. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-india-57167329 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[India]] reports a record 4,329 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 278,719. [https://m.timesofindia.com/india/covid-19-india-reports-4329-deaths-in-24-hours-biggest-single-day-toll-over-2-63-lakh-cases-in-a-day/amp_articleshow/82728818.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 47 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 1,994. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2021/05/18/4865-covid-19-cases-selangor-has-most-infections/ (Free Malaysia Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Singapore]]
****The [[Singapore]]an [[Health Sciences Authority]] approves the use of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] for children between the ages of 12 and 15. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/05/18/singapore-approves-covid-vaccine-for-children-outlines-vaccination-plan.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****[[Taipei]] and [[New Taipei City]] close all [[Elementary school|elementary]], [[Middle school|middle]], and [[high school]]s until May 28 amidst an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/05/aab158a1e552-taipei-schools-to-close-as-coronavirus-cases-increase-in-taiwan.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 35 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 649. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-thailand-reports-daily-record-of-35-new-deaths-14831052 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] reports records of 35,543 new cases of COVID-19 and 745 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the total number of cases to 3.37 million and the death toll to 71,771. [https://www.minutouno.com/sociedad/coronavirus-argentina/record-total-del-35543-casos-y-745-muertos-un-dia-n5193539 (''Minuto Uno'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
***[[Austria]] announces that they will phase out the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] from its [[COVID-19 vaccination|vaccination programme]] because of delivery problems and wariness among the population following reports of the vaccine's rare side-effects. [https://www.thelocal.at/20210518/austria-to-phase-out-astrazeneca-vaccine/ (''The Local Austria'')]
*The [[United States Preventive Services Task Force|U.S. Preventive Services Task Force]] lowers the age to begin routine screenings for [[colorectal cancer]] from 50 to 45. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/health/2021/05/18/colorectal-cancer-uspstf-guidelines-say-begin-screening-45-not-50/5074671001/ (''USA Today'')] [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/colon-cancer-screening-should-start-age-45-us-task-force-2021-05-18/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[European migrant crisis]], [[Morocco–Spain relations]]
**[[Spain]] deploys the [[Spanish Army|Army]] in [[Ceuta]] to control [[Morocco–Spain border|the border]] with [[Morocco]] while [[Immigration to Spain|immigrants]] continue to arrive in the face of the permissiveness of the [[Law enforcement in Morocco|Moroccan police]]. At least one migrant is reported dead while trying to cross the border in [[Melilla]]. [https://english.elpais.com/spanish_news/2021-05-18/more-than-6000-people-swim-to-ceuta-amid-diplomatic-row-between-spain-and-morocco.html (''El País'' in English)]
**The mayor-president of Ceuta [[Juan Jesús Vivas]] calls the situation an "invasion" and announces the suspension of the vaccination campaign against COVID-19 for Wednesday as the city is experiencing a "state of emergency atmosphere". [https://www.20minutos.es/noticia/4699841/0/el-presidente-de-ceuta-dice-que-la-ciudad-vive-un-estado-de-excepcion-por-la-crisis-migratoria-y-suspende-la-vacunacion/ (20 minutos)]
**Spanish [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Spain)|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Arancha González Laya]] summons the Moroccan ambassador, who is later recalled to [[Rabat]] for consultations. Ambassador Karima Benyaich advises that "there are actions that have consequences, and they have to be assumed", referring to the fact that the Polisario leader is receiving treatment for COVID-19 in Spain. [https://www.europapress.es/nacional/noticia-exteriores-convoca-embajadora-marruecos-llegada-masiva-migrantes-ceuta-20210518143036.html (''Europa Press'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-57156320 (BBC News)]
*[[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea]]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] issues a [[gag order]] that forbids his [[Cabinet of the Philippines|cabinet]] from publicly discussing the [[South China Sea]] dispute, which comes after some of his secretaries criticized the [[government of China]] over the presence of Chinese vessels in the [[exclusive economic zone of the Philippines]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/18/philippines-duterte-issues-gag-order-over-south-china-sea (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Lebanon–Saudi Arabia relations]], [[Lebanon–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[Saudi Arabia]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]] both summon their [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] ambassadors after Lebanese Foreign Minister [[Charbel Wehbe]] accused the [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf States]] of playing a role in the rise of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]] in a heated exchange with a [[Saudis|Saudi]] guest during an interview yesterday. Wehbe has since apologized for his remarks. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/18/saudi-arabia-summons-lebanons-envoy-over-ministers-remarks (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Libya–Tunisia relations]]
**[[Tunisia]]'s flag carrier [[Tunisair]] announces that it has resumed services to [[Libya]] in light of the UN-sponsored [[Libyan peace process|peace agreement]], becoming the first foreign airline to connect to the country since the outbreak of the [[Second Libyan Civil War]] seven years ago. Yesterday, the airline flew its first flights to [[Benghazi]] and [[Tripoli, Libya|Tripoli]], and it has scheduled five flights to both cities each week. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/18/tunisair-first-foreign-carrier-to-resume-libya-flights (Al Jazeera)] 

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Xenophobia and racism related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] votes 364–62 to pass the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act. The bill, which would expedite anti-Asian hate crime reviews to the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]], will head to [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] for his signature. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/house-poised-final-passage-anti-asian-hate-crimes/story?id=77756120 (ABC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[International protests over the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
***[[Arab Americans]] in [[Dearborn, Michigan]], stage a protest across the city during a visit by [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] to the [[Ford River Rouge Complex]] over the [[United States]]' support of [[Israel]]'s response to attacks from [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.freep.com/story/news/local/michigan/wayne/2021/05/18/joe-biden-speech-dearborn-protests-israel-live-stream/5142308001/ (''Detroit Free Press'')]
***[[Indonesians]] gather at the [[Embassy of the United States, Jakarta|U.S. Embassy]] in [[Jakarta]] to stand in solidarity with [[Palestinians|Palestine]] and demand an end to Israeli airstrikes in Gaza. [https://apnews.com/article/united-nations-indonesia-middle-east-israel-israel-palestinian-conflict-50870446318e3e01fae71816791c58df (AP)]
**Palestinians in the [[West Bank]], [[East Jerusalem]], and communities inside Israel hold a [[general strike]] to protest Israel's [[bombardment]] of the Gaza Strip and the [[eviction]]s of Palestinians in [[Sheikh Jarrah]]. The [[Central Committee of Fatah]] calls it a "day of rage". [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/palestinians-stage-nation-wide-general-strike (Middle East Eye)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Transgender people in sports]]
**The [[French Rugby Federation]] allows [[trans women]] players to feature in top-level [[women's rugby union]] in [[Rugby union in France|the country]] starting next season, overturning [[World Rugby]]'s advice against this. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/05/18/sport/transgender-women-rugby-france-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
